name: Peripheral Lembata
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Keraf, Gregorius. 1978. Morfologi Dialek Lamalera. PhD diss., Universitas Indonesia (grammar of Lamalera = Peripheral Lembata; print only, no digital copy found). Fricke 2019 Leiden thesis download blocked by bot wall.
earlier_scan.note: Keraf 1978 is the only full grammar; check its fonologi chapter for tekanan (stress).

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste. Berlin: Language Science Press (LSP 526).
sources.note: Lamalera [lmr] appears only in the classification tree (Peripheral Lembata Lamaholot: Kawela, Lebatukan, Lamalera) and comparative word tables; the sole stress remark is areal (sec. 3.2.1): 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables.' Not language-specific.

sources.citation: Magi Krova, Magdalena. 2018. Analisis Morfofonemik Dialek Lamalera. JPNM: Jurnal Pustaka Nusantara Multidisiplin 3(2), 7 pp. (Garuda record 4508602, dated 2024).
sources.note: Indonesian; morphophonemics of possessive nasal vowels and 'pemanjangan vokal pada suku kata sebelumnya' (vowel lengthening in the preceding syllable); the word 'tekanan' does not occur.

sources.citation: Michels, Marc. 2017. Western Lamaholot: A cross-dialectal grammar sketch. Research MA thesis, Universiteit Leiden.
sources.note: Sec. 2.2.1 p.25: 'Stress in Lamaholot is not usually contrastive. The general rule is that stress is on the penultimate syllable, but even neighbouring dialects may vary in the details'... 'Rather less is known about stress in most dialects outside of Flores.' Lamalera is cited only for vowel length (Keraf 1978); no Lamalera stress data.

sources.citation: Kroon, Yosep Bisara. 2016. A grammar of Solor-Lamaholot. PhD thesis, University of Adelaide.
sources.note: Sec. 3.4 (p.52) stress statement is for Solor only; sec. 2.3.1 summarises Keraf 1978 as a morphological study with 33-dialect lexicostatistics; Lamalera cited for s~h alternation biso [`biso] ~ biho (Keraf 1978) with Kroon's own stress mark, not a rule.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record lama1278 (MED: Keraf 1978, long_grammar).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; three descriptive refs (Keraf 1978; Manggarani 2013 MA Leiden; Demon 2006 MA Udayana).

sources.citation: LexiRumah 3 (Kaiping, Edwards & Klamer), forms for lects lama1277-lamal/-mulan/-belan/-wuake/-lamah/-merde, all sourced to Keraf 1978.
sources.note: 1199 wordlist forms; no stress marks in the digitised Keraf 1978 lists.

sources.citation: Demon, Yosef. 2022. Morphophonemics in the Lamalera Dialect of Lamaholot. Randwick International of Education and Linguistics Science Journal 3(1): 112-127. doi:10.47175/rielsj.v3i1.414
sources.note: Nothing on stress; clitic-driven sound replacement/insertion/elision only. States Lamaholot is 'not tonal' (abstract, p.112). No 'stress', 'tekanan', 'accent' or 'syllable' prominence anywhere in the text.

sources.citation: Demon, Yosef & Veronika Genua. 2021. Inflexive Marker and Morphophonological Processes in the Lamalera Dialect of Lamaholot Language (LDLL). RIELS Journal 2(3): 383-396. doi:10.47175/rielsj.v2i3.306
sources.note: Nothing on stress; pronominal proclitic/enclitic morphophonology; remarks on vowel lengthening/gemination only (p.391).

sources.citation: Fricke, Hanna L. A. 2019. Traces of language contact: The Flores-Lembata languages in eastern Indonesia. LOT 544. Utrecht: LOT (Leiden PhD).
sources.note: Sec. 3.2.5 (p.49) 'Stress in Central Lembata... the penultimate syllable of the word is stressed, unless the penultimate contains the vowel schwa' is for Central Lembata (levu1239), not this language. For Lamalera she only reports Keraf 1978a as the morphology source (p.158; Table 7.1 p.273) and uses his wordlists; no Lamalera stress statement.

sources.citation: Demon, Yosef. 2017. Pragmatic alternative construction (fronting, left dislocation, and topicalization) in Lamalera dialect. RETORIKA: Jurnal Ilmu Bahasa 3(2): 240-246. doi:10.22225/jr.3.2.338.240-246
Demon, Yosef. 2017. The Marking System in the Dialect of Lamalera. International Journal of Language and Linguistics 5(4): 105-120.
